subject: Two-state SNP predictors/effects in DOQTL v rqtl2

messages.author: 2c7106159c8e6d5b
messages.subject: Two-state SNP predictors/effects in DOQTL v rqtl2
parts:
Hi Karl,

Please tell me if I have this right...

In legacy DOQTL, conversion from 8-state founder dosages to 2-state allelic/SNP dosages produced a genetic predictor range [0,2], basically a continuous estimate of the number of reference alleles at a marker. As a result, for a DOQTL mixed model with SNP dosages, the coefficient for a unit change in the marker predictor is an additive effect of allele substitution (adding one more reference allele).

A similar conversion in qtl2 produces a reference (major?) allele value range [0,1], basically the proportion of reference alleles at a marker. So, unless there is something that happens inside scan1 itself, a unit change in the predictor is the change from homozygous alternative to homozygous reference, effectively twice the effect from DOQTL. 

There is some language in your 2018 paper that is consistent with this interpretation. In both cases I'm assuming a model with additive effects only. 

Thanks for any clarification.

David

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Two-state SNP predictors/effects in DOQTL v rqtl2
parts:
Converting from 36-state probabilities -> 8 allele dosages -> 2 SNP
dosages, in R/qtl2 it's always that the sum of the probabilities for an
individual at a given position is 1.

karl
